newsitem.title: GERMANY: Deutsche Telekom in TV talks with Kirch.
newsitem.headline: Deutsche Telekom in TV talks with Kirch.

text.p: German telecommunications giant Deutsche Telekom AG (DT) and Bavarian media mogul Leo Kirch are in talks about cooperating in the development of digital pay television, a German newspaper reported on Monday.

In an interview with the economic daily Handelsblatt newspaper, DT chairman Ron Sommer said the goal of the talks with the Kirch Group was to increase the amount of programming in Telekom's loss-making cable television network.
"Next to us, they have invested the most in this business," Sommer said.
He added that DT was seeking normal business relations with Kirch, but did not rule out a pay TV joint venture in future.
Last month DT said it would withdraw from another pay TV alliance, Multimedia Betriebsgesellschaft (MMBG), in which it was partners with Kirch rival Bertelsmann.
Sommer said he expected MMBG would fold by the end of the year.

DT is the largest MMBG shareholder with a direct stake of 27 percent and another 18.5 percent in trusteeship. Bertelsmann holds 5.5 percent through its subsidiary Ufa Film und Fernseh GmbH, 5.5 percent through television network RTL and 11 percent through Cie Luxembourgoise de Telediffusion (CLT). CLT and Ufa are set to merge later this year.

Sommer said DT would step up modernisation of the cable television network, which broadcasts to some 16.2 million homes in Germany. Of that total, DT actually has just over 5 million under contract. The rest are serviced by alternative cable companies.

The alternative cable TV companies have called for a total investment of five billion marks ($3.3 billion) to upgrade the cable TV network for interactive programming and telephone service, but Sommer rejected these proposals.
"Why should we throw money out the window for something that we already have," he asked.
The networks of the alternative cable companies could be a potential threat to DT in local phone services when the telecommunications market is deregulated in 1998.
But in order for them to offer these services, DT must upgrade the national backbone cable network.
-- William Boston, Bonn Newsroom, 49 228 26097150 ($ = 1.529 German Marks)
